Random sampling counters automation bias by ensuring that not all investigations are based solely on high-risk signals generated by algorithms. By incorporating a random sample into the fraud detection process, inspectors are encouraged to critically evaluate cases rather than relying blindly on algorithmic results. This approach helps to monitor and mitigate risks of discrimination, as it allows for the tracking of whether certain groups are disproportionately represented in algorithmic outcomes.

Regarding the AI Act duties for high-risk providers, the use of random sampling is relevant because high-risk AI systems are required to identify and mitigate foreseeable risks, including potential discrimination. The random sample can serve as a control tool to ensure compliance with these obligations, as it provides a means to assess the performance and fairness of the algorithm in a structured manner. This aligns with the AI Act's emphasis on transparency and accountability in the deployment of high-risk AI systems.
